title: How are horses helping to heal humans?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: term used to describe a large number of different things which all belong to a single common category
brushing and cleaning the coat of hair of a horse, dog or other animal
stage of life when a child grows into an adult because of changes in their body which allow them to have children
(child) who is looked after by the local authorities because they cannot be cared for by their parents or family; also known as a 'looked after child'
strong feeling of reliance and confidence between two people

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. Neil, have you ever ridden a horse?
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Georgie。Neil，你骑过马吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I have. I can't say that I enjoyed it much.
sentences.zh: 是的，我骑过。但我不能说我很享受。

sentences.en: I was a bit scared to be honest. How about you?
sentences.zh: 说实话，我当时有点害怕。你呢？

sentences.en: I used to ride horses a lot actually. My favourite thing was to ride a horse through the countryside.
sentences.zh: 实际上我以前经常骑马。我最喜欢骑着马穿过乡间。

sentences.en: I love horses. They're so majestic and lovely.
sentences.zh: 我爱马。它们是如此雄伟且可爱。

sentences.en: The relationship between humans and horses has been close throughout history, but recently this has gone beyond riding horses for fun or using them for work.
sentences.zh: 纵观历史，人类与马的关系一直很亲密，但最近这种关系已经超越了为了好玩而骑马或将其用于劳作。

sentences.en: Equine Assisted Services, sometimes called horse therapy, is a health trend where caring and interacting with horses is used to heal physical and mental illness.
sentences.zh: 马匹辅助服务（Equine Assisted Services），有时也被称为马匹疗法，是一种健康趋势，通过照顾马匹并与之互动来治愈身心疾病。

sentences.en: Here's Datshiane Navanayaga, presenter of BBC World Service programme The Conversation, to explain: Equine Assisted Services is now an umbrella term which encompasses a whole range of treatments, involving activities and interactions with horses to promote better human wellbeing.
sentences.zh: 下面由 BBC World Service 节目 The Conversation 的主持人 Datshiane Navanayaga 来解释：马匹辅助服务现在是一个总称，涵盖了一系列治疗方法，涉及与马的活动和互动，以促进人类的身心健康。

sentences.en: Equine Assisted Services is an umbrella term – a term for a large number of different things which all belong to a single common category.
sentences.zh: 马匹辅助服务是一个总称（umbrella term）——指代属于同一个大类下的许多不同事物的术语。

sentences.en: So, horse therapy includes many activities, from feeling the horse's movement, which can help children with muscle disorders like cerebral palsy, to simply grooming the horse, which can help calm anxiety.
sentences.zh: 因此，马匹疗法包括许多活动，从感受马的运动（这可以帮助患有脑瘫等肌肉障碍的儿童），到简单的刷马（这可以帮助缓解焦虑）。

sentences.en: Grooming a horse means cleaning and brushing the horse's coat of hair.
sentences.zh: 刷马（Grooming）是指清洁和刷理马的皮毛。

sentences.en: Various animals can be used in therapy, but horses are particularly suitable as they're very sensitive to human emotions.
sentences.zh: 各种动物都可以用于治疗，但马特别合适，因为它们对人类的情绪非常敏感。

sentences.en: Being in contact with them affects the limbic area of the brain, dealing with stress.
sentences.zh: 与它们接触会影响大脑中处理压力的边缘系统区域。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll hear more about the horses helping people work through mental, emotional and physical challenges.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将听到更多关于马如何帮助人们克服心理、情感和身体挑战的故事。

sentences.en: And, as usual, we'll learn some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们将学习一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all the words and phrases from this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com But now I have a question for you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的所有单词和短语。但现在我有一个问题要问你，Neil。

sentences.en: We've heard some of the special qualities horses possess, but which of the following about horses is also true?
sentences.zh: 我们已经听说了一些马具备的特殊品质，但关于马的以下哪项描述也是正确的？

sentences.en: Is it: a) horses always sleep standing up, b) horses can make over 100 sounds, or c) horses have almost 360-degree vision?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 马总是站着睡觉，b) 马能发出 100 多种声音，还是 c) 马拥有近 360 度的视野？

sentences.en: Well, I'm sure I've seen a horse lying down so...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确定我见过马躺下，所以……

sentences.en: I don't know about its vision though, so I'm going to say b) a horse can make over 100 sounds.
sentences.zh: 不过我不太了解它的视野，所以我选 b) 马能发出 100 多种声音。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。稍后我们将在节目中揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Horse therapist Claudia Nicholson first felt the healing power of horses as a child.
sentences.zh: 马匹治疗师 Claudia Nicholson 在孩提时代就第一次感受到了马的治愈力量。

sentences.en: She now runs her own centre for Equine Assisted Learning in the south of England, where she spoke with BBC World Service programme The Conversation.
sentences.zh: 她现在在英格兰南部经营着自己的马匹辅助学习中心，她在那里接受了 BBC World Service 节目 The Conversation 的采访。

sentences.en: I would spend hours on end sitting in a stable with my pony.
sentences.zh: 我会连续几个小时坐在马厩里陪着我的小马。

sentences.en: I was going through puberty, my parents had separated, I had a lot of unanswered questions, and I would feel met and safe and held with the connection of the pony.
sentences.zh: 当时我正处于青春期，父母分居了，我有很多解不开的疑问，而通过与小马的这种连接，我感到被理解、安全且被呵护。

sentences.en: As a child, Claudia spent hours on end with her pony.
sentences.zh: 孩提时，Claudia 会连续几个小时和小马待在一起。

sentences.en: Phrases like days or hours on end mean days or hours doing something continuously, without stopping.
sentences.zh: 像 days or hours on end 这样的短语意思是连续几天或几小时做某事，不停歇。

sentences.en: Spending time with her pony helped Claudia through puberty – the stage of life when a child grows into an adult because of changes in their body which allow them to have children.
sentences.zh: 与小马相处的时光帮助 Claudia 度过了青春期（puberty）——即孩子由于身体变化而成长为成年人，并具备生育能力的生命阶段。

sentences.en: It was her teenage experiences that led Claudia to start her own horse therapy centre.
sentences.zh: 正是青少年时期的经历促使 Claudia 创办了自己的马匹治疗中心。

sentences.en: She works a lot with teenage girls and children in care.
sentences.zh: 她经常与青春期少女和受照管儿童一起工作。

sentences.en: A child in care is a child who's being looked after by the local authorities because they cannot be cared for by their parents or family.
sentences.zh: 受照管儿童（child in care）是指由地方当局照顾的孩子，因为他们的父母或家人无法照顾他们。

sentences.en: Here, Claudia talks more about her work with children and horses to BBC World Service's The Conversation: It will take maybe a few sessions for a relationship of trust to be formed, and it's quite extraordinary to see a child that's experienced a lot of trauma, especially in these children in care.They can be brushing the pony's body.
sentences.zh: 在这里，Claudia 向 BBC World Service 的 The Conversation 进一步讲述了她与孩子和马的工作：建立信任关系可能需要几次疗程，看到一个经历过很多创伤的孩子，尤其是这些受照管儿童，是非常了不起的。他们可能会刷着小马的身体。

sentences.en: They might want to have a cry which they've been holding on to.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会想哭出来，那是他们一直压抑着的情绪。

sentences.en: The horse regulates them. Many of the children Claudia works with suffer trauma.
sentences.zh: 马能调节他们的情绪。许多与 Claudia 一起工作的孩子都遭受过创伤。

sentences.en: It takes time for them to build a bond of trust with their horse.
sentences.zh: 他们需要时间与马建立信任纽带。

sentences.en: The phrase bond of trust is a strong feeling of reliance and confidence between two people.
sentences.zh: 信任纽带（bond of trust）是指两人之间强烈的依赖感和信心。

sentences.en: Horses really are special animals. They sense human feelings like fear or sadness through breath, heart rate and movement, and respond with gentleness and calm.
sentences.zh: 马确实是特殊的动物。它们通过呼吸、心率和动作感知人类的情绪，如恐惧或悲伤，并以温柔和冷静作为回应。

sentences.en: This makes them perfect animal therapists.
sentences.zh: 这使它们成为完美的动物治疗师。

sentences.en: And that's not all! Right, Georgie? Let's find out the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 而且还不止于此！对吧，Georgie？让我们来看看你那个问题的答案。

sentences.en: Yes, Neil. Well, I asked you which sentence about horses was true, and you said that horses can make over 100 sounds...
sentences.zh: 是的，Neil。我问你关于马的哪句话是正确的，你说马能发出 100 多种声音……

sentences.en: Sadly, that was the wrong answer. The correct answer was c) horses have near 360-degree vision, which is surprising.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，那是错误答案。正确答案是 c) 马拥有近 360 度的视野，这很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Wow. That's amazing! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with umbrella term – a term used to describe many different things which all belong to a single common category.
sentences.zh: 哇。太神奇了！好了。让我们回顾一下学过的词汇，首先是总称（umbrella term）——用于描述属于同一个大类下的许多不同事物的术语。

sentences.en: Grooming an animal, like a horse or a dog, means brushing and cleaning its coat of hair.
sentences.zh: 刷理（Grooming）动物，如马或狗，是指刷洗和清洁它的皮毛。

sentences.en: If you do something for hours on end, you do it continuously, without stopping.
sentences.zh: 如果你连续几个小时（for hours on end）做某事，意思是你不停地连续做这件事。

sentences.en: Puberty is the stage of life when a child grows into an adult because of changes in their body which allow them to have children.
sentences.zh: 青春期（Puberty）是孩子由于身体变化而成长为成年人，并具备生育能力的生命阶段。

sentences.en: A child who is in care is being looked after by the local authorities because they cannot be cared for by their parents.
sentences.zh: 受照管（in care）的孩子是指由地方当局照顾的孩子，因为他们的父母无法照顾他们。

sentences.en: And finally, a bond of trust is a strong feeling of reliance and confidence between two people.
sentences.zh: 最后，信任纽带（bond of trust）是指两人之间强烈的依赖感和信心。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember you'll find a quiz and worksheet for this episode over on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但记住你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的测验和工作单。

sentences.en: See you there soon, but for now it's goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快再见，现在要说再见了！

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
